problem: End-to-end RL ObjectNav methods learn contextual relations only implicitly and lack geometry, while modular map-based methods record observed geometry but lack reasoning about contextual object relations, limiting exploration efficiency.
motivation: In unseen environments the agent must infer unobserved contextual objects from partial observations to deduce where the target likely is. An explicit, geometry-aware representation of unknown regions could make goal selection more efficient.
key_idea: Train a self-supervised generative map (SGM) to reconstruct masked pixels of a cropped global semantic map using episodic observations and general knowledge, then use the generated map to predict the target location as the navigation goal.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that explicitly imagining unobserved map regions through self-supervised masked reconstruction injects contextual reasoning into a modular geometry-preserving pipeline.
method: Self-supervised generative map (SGM): trained to reconstruct masked pixels of a cropped global semantic map, using both episodic observations and general knowledge.
Incomplete local semantic map: the agent maintains a partial local semantic map of the observed geometry during navigation.
Map generation: the pretrained SGM fills in the unknown regions of the local map.
Goal selection: the predicted target location on the generated map is set as the goal and the agent moves towards it.

setting.backbone: Self-supervised generative map model (masked map reconstruction) within a modular mapping pipeline
setting.training_data: Cropped global semantic maps with masked pixels (self-supervised); exact scale not given in the abstract
setting.observation: not stated in the abstract (semantic local map built from egocentric observations)
setting.action_space: not stated in the abstract (modular method moving towards a map goal)
